items.title: Registered unit test calls logic.process() with the wrong signature and will fail

findings.title: Registered unit test calls logic.process() with the wrong signature and will fail
findings.explanation: process() is defined as process(self, centerlineCurve, inputModel, outputModel, radius, length, position, numberOfTubes, resolution, showResult=True) (lines 1403-1412), so this call passes only 5 of 8 required positional arguments and raises TypeError. EVARSim/CMakeLists.txt line 27 registers this class as a ctest (slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT ${MODULE_NAME}.py)), so the extension's test step fails and the core geometry code is effectively untested.
findings.suggestion: Update the test to the current signature, e.g. logic.process(centerlineCurve, None, outputModel, radius, length, 0.0, 1, resolution), and add a second case using a polyline model input.

findings.title: Bundled unit test calls process() with wrong arguments and fails
findings.explanation: test_EVARSim1 calls logic.process with 5 positional arguments, but process requires at least 8 (centerlineCurve, inputModel, outputModel, radius, length, position, numberOfTubes, resolution). The call raises TypeError. The test is registered via slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT EVARSim.py) in EVARSim/CMakeLists.txt, so ctest for the extension fails. It also never checks branch or multi-tube behavior.
findings.suggestion: Update the test to the current signature, e.g. logic.process(centerlineCurve, None, outputModel, 2.0, 10.0, 0.5, 1, 16), and add assertions for the input-model path and multi-tube output.

items.title: Additional tubes are placed along tube 1's reduced segment, not the full centerline

findings.title: Additional tubes are placed along tube 1's reduced segment, not the full centerline
findings.explanation: reducedPoints is the 4-point spline of the already positioned segment for tube 1 (lines 1475-1479). _createAdditionalTubes then distributes positions 0.2-0.8 along that short segment (line 1130), so tubes 2..N are stacked inside tube 1's span instead of being spread along the vessel; with the default length of 10 mm and a long centerline the extra stents overlap almost completely.
findings.suggestion: Pass the full (smoothed) curvePoints to _createAdditionalTubes and let each tube position itself along the whole centerline.

items.title: Branch selection ignored in the process() path

findings.title: Branch selection ignored in the process() path
findings.evidence:
# Get the first line segment (or could be modified to use branch selection)
                  lines = polyData.GetLines()
findings.explanation: The widget applies the selected branch through _extractBranchCenterline, but process() always takes the first line cell of an input model. A headless caller of process() therefore gets a different branch from the GUI for the same input.
findings.suggestion: Pass the branch index into process() and reuse _extractBranchCenterline so both paths match.

items.title: Division by zero on duplicate centerline points

findings.title: Division by zero on duplicate centerline points
findings.explanation: segmentLengths[i] is zero when two consecutive curve points coincide (common in imported polylines), producing inf/nan points; the same risk exists in _addRigidEndCaps (line 904, 909) and _createCircularCap (line 935) where a zero-length direction vector is normalized. In process() this surfaces as a confusing error or an empty/garbage model rather than a clear message.
findings.suggestion: Skip zero-length segments and guard the normalizations with a length check.

items.title: Errors swallowed with print() instead of being reported to the user

findings.title: Errors swallowed with print() instead of being reported to the user
findings.explanation: _updateSelectedTube, _analyzeBranches, _createBranchLabels, _removeBranchLabels, _extractBranchCenterline, _smoothCenterline, _reduceCenterlinePoints and _applySplineSmoothing all catch Exception and only print to stdout. In a GUI session the user sees nothing when, for example, branch extraction fails, and the module appears to do nothing; the same pattern also hides real bugs from the test suite.
findings.suggestion: Report failures via slicer.util.errorDisplay or logging.warning, and let unexpected exceptions propagate to the tryWithErrorDisplay wrapper in onApplyButton.

findings.title: Errors swallowed with console print instead of user-visible reporting
findings.evidence:
except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error updating selected tube: {e}")
findings.explanation: Several broad except blocks print the exception and continue, so a failing tube update or branch analysis leaves the GUI silently stale. Users see no error dialog or status message.
findings.suggestion: Report failures via slicer.util.errorDisplay or logging.error and keep the GUI state consistent.

findings.title: No clinical-use or simulation-only disclaimer
findings.evidence: This module allows users to place endovascular devices along centerline curves for EVAR (Endovascular Aneurysm Repair) simulation.
findings.explanation: The module simulates endovascular stent placement for EVAR, a clinical procedure. The help text and README do not state that output is not validated for clinical decisions or planning. Users could misread the simulation as clinically accurate.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit research-only / not-for-clinical-use disclaimer to helpText and README.

items.title: No validation or clinical-use disclaimer for a device-sizing simulation tool

findings.title: No validation or clinical-use disclaimer for a device-sizing simulation tool
findings.evidence: See License.txt. This extension is developed for medical research and educational purposes.
findings.explanation: The module produces stent geometry from centerlines that users may interpret as sizing information, yet there is no statement that results are not validated for clinical decision making, no accuracy/validation data, and the license pointer names a file that does not exist (the file is LICENSE).
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit research-only / not-for-clinical-use disclaimer, state the intended accuracy and validation status, and fix the license filename reference.

findings.title: README references nonexistent License.txt
findings.evidence: See License.txt. This extension is developed for medical research and educational purposes.
findings.explanation: The README says the license is in License.txt, but the repository only has LICENSE (Apache-2.0). Users may be unable to find the terms. Low impact; the LICENSE file itself is present and permissive.
findings.suggestion: Change the reference to LICENSE (Apache-2.0).

items.title: README instructions and parameter ranges disagree with the module

findings.title: README instructions and parameter ranges disagree with the module
findings.evidence: Find "EVARSim" in the module dropdown under the "Examples" category
findings.explanation: The module registers itself under the 'Modeling' category (EVARSim.py line 33) and the UI allows radius 0.1-50, length 0.1-200 and resolution 6-64, while the README says 'Examples', radius 0.1-10.0, length 1.0-200 and resolution 4-32. Users following the README will look in the wrong category and expect different limits.
findings.suggestion: Update the README to match the implemented category and slider ranges.

items.title: Sample data CL_model.vtk is committed but not installed by CMake

findings.title: Sample data CL_model.vtk is committed but not installed by CMake
findings.explanation: MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES lists only the icon and the .ui file, so EVARSim/CL_model.vtk (290 KB) is not copied into the installed extension. README line 122 states 'The extension includes `CL_model.vtk` - a sample branched centerline file of the aorta and the aortic bifurcation.', which is false for users who install from the extension manager; they have no sample data to try the module with.
findings.suggestion: Either install the file (add it to MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES / a data directory) or register it as Sample Data, or remove the claim from the README.

items.title: Scene nodes are deleted by name, which can remove user-created nodes

findings.title: Scene nodes are deleted by name, which can remove user-created nodes
findings.explanation: _clearExistingTubes removes any node named EVARSim_Tube_2..EVARSim_Tube_10 and _removeBranchLabels removes any node whose name starts with 'EVARSim_BranchLabel_' (line 592). If a user renamed their own model or fiducial to such a name, pressing Apply or changing the input model deletes it without confirmation.
findings.suggestion: Track the created nodes in the parameter node or a member list and remove only those instances.

items.title: Selecting an input model silently adds fiducial nodes to the scene

findings.title: Selecting an input model silently adds fiducial nodes to the scene
findings.explanation: _onInputModelChanged calls _analyzeBranches, which calls _createBranchLabels and inserts one markup fiducial per detected line segment into the user's scene. Merely choosing an input model therefore modifies the scene (and the saved .mrrl if the user saves), which is unexpected and can pollute a clinical scene.
findings.suggestion: Make branch labels opt-in via a checkbox, or use a single non-persistent display node / 3D text actor instead of MRML nodes.

items.title: Smoothing-factor slider has no effect on Apply

findings.title: Smoothing-factor slider has no effect on Apply
findings.evidence: smoothingFactor = 0.3  # Default smoothing factor for the process method
findings.explanation: The GUI exposes a smoothingFactor slider (UI lines 331-350, parameter node line 86) and the live preview uses it, but onApplyButton() (lines 602-611) never passes it to process(), which hardcodes 0.3. A user who sets smoothing to 0 or 1 and presses Apply silently gets 0.3, so the applied result differs from the preview.
findings.suggestion: Add a smoothingFactor argument to process() and pass self.ui.smoothingFactorSliderWidget.value from onApplyButton().

items.title: Stale compiled bytecode committed to the repository

findings.title: Stale compiled bytecode committed to the repository
findings.explanation: A 36 KB Python 3.9 bytecode cache of the module is checked in and .gitignore only lists '.DS_Store' and '.git'. It is not installed by CMake so it does not shadow the source, but it is a stale binary artifact that can drift from EVARSim.py and confuses review of what actually runs.
findings.suggestion: Remove EVARSim/__pycache__ from the repository and add '__pycache__/' and '*.pyc' to .gitignore.

findings.title: Compiled bytecode and large sample binary committed to repository
findings.explanation: EVARSim/__pycache__/EVARSim.cpython-39.pyc (36 KB) is a generated artifact that is committed, and .gitignore does not exclude it. The 290 KB CL_model.vtk sample is also committed. The bytecode may be stale against the source and adds clutter to the extension source.
findings.suggestion: Remove __pycache__ from the repository, add it to .gitignore, and keep sample data only if it is needed by the documented workflow.

items.title: Unused and dead code paths referencing wrong signatures

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports left in the module
findings.evidence: def _createMultipleTubes(self, curvePoints: vtk.vtkPoints, radius: float, length: float,
findings.explanation: _createMultipleTubes (line 980) and _createSeparateTubes (line 1055) are never called, and numpy is imported but unused in _extractCenterlineFromModel (line 641). This makes the actual behaviour harder to follow for reviewers and future maintainers.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unused methods and imports, or wire them up if they are intended features.

findings.title: Unused and dead code paths referencing wrong signatures
findings.evidence: def _createMultipleTubes(self, curvePoints: vtk.vtkPoints, radius: float, length: float,
findings.explanation: _createMultipleTubes, _createSeparateTubes, and _createAdditionalTubes are not called from the current flow or have mismatched parameters. The dead code increases maintenance risk and hides the test mismatch.
findings.suggestion: Remove dead helpers or consolidate tube creation into one code path.

items.title: process() assumes a 3D view exists when showResult is True

findings.title: process() assumes a 3D view exists when showResult is True
findings.explanation: If the user has a layout without a 3D view (e.g. only slice views), threeDWidget(0) returns None and threeDView.resetFocalPoint() raises AttributeError after the model was already created, so the operation reports failure even though it succeeded.
findings.suggestion: Check threeDWidget for None before calling resetFocalPoint().

items.title: Full geometry rebuild on every slider tick runs on the GUI thread

findings.title: Full geometry rebuild on every slider tick runs on the GUI thread
findings.explanation: Each slider movement triggers _updateSelectedTube, which re-extracts/smooths the centerline and rebuilds the tube synchronously in the GUI thread; with a large input model (the O(points x 20 slices) scan in _findCenterAtLevel) the UI will freeze while dragging.
findings.suggestion: Debounce the preview (e.g. QTimer) or move the computation to a background thread with progress reporting.

items.title: Integer-valued parameters typed as float in the parameter node

findings.title: Integer-valued parameters typed as float in the parameter node
findings.explanation: numberOfTubes and cylinderResolution are counts but are declared as float and converted with int() at every use site (lines 269, 609-610), which is fragile if a non-integral value ever reaches them.
findings.suggestion: Use Annotated[int, WithinRange(1, 10)] and Annotated[int, WithinRange(6, 64)].
